review_note: Owned demand and customer economics are the minimum concepts needed before buying more demand; CAC/payback is conditional on available numbers.
The case requires traffic-state coherence, real differentiation and offer/CTA diagnosis before UI micro-optimization.
Buyer/user separation plus market validity, reachability and customer economics are all decision-relevant; a relationship-origin sale is insufficient market proof.
Price objection must be diagnosed through target fit, difference and economic price testing; proof specificity can strengthen but is not always independently required.
A new product must pass market validity and must not be used to replicate a weak core; the growth unit already includes economics/capacity prerequisites.
The decision hinges on working already-paid-for opportunity inventory before cold acquisition.
The founder bottleneck case is fundamentally a transferability/process problem before hiring capacity.
Need duration, experience/result and the next-transaction bridge to distinguish churn from natural expiry and choose retention/second-sale/referral coherently.
Channel selection requires demand hierarchy, identifiable target and the amount of education/urgency before choosing Meta or any platform.
Low close rate requires prequalification/decision process, diagnostic selling and certainty/value/price-gap checks before more closing pressure.
Revenue vs cash requires CAC/margin/payback/capital mechanics plus customer-level profitability.
The answer must separate Merenda customer-appropriateness doctrine from the assimilated Proof by Refusal contribution and preserve real authorship.
The case is explicitly about zero-based reconstruction and sunk-cost/legacy classification.
Lead quality must be defined economically, source must be separated from prospect state, and routing/process diagnosed before changing platform.
CRM is downstream of a designed process with states, triggers, next action, owner and human-intervention rules.
Distribution requires both the two-audience sell-in/sell-through distinction and execution/support of the partner channel.
The core decision is funnel depth by intent, urgency, complexity and information/fiduciary need, not B2B as a label.
Search volume is only a signal; buying intent, market validity and economic customer quality remain required before offer construction.
The hidden high-leverage concept is that acquisition constraints change the economic/commercial mix rather than merely requiring a substitute media channel.
Five-star reviews are an asset, but generic satisfaction, credibility/proof, authority/trust and differentiation are distinct jobs.
Current channel doctrine makes analog conditional on function, demand, intent, target and economics rather than a universal requirement.
Premium means a sustainable profitable price gap grounded in difference/proof/economics, not numerically highest price by dogma.
Followers/views must be translated into observable economic progression and distinguished from demand and economically desirable customers.
Automation must follow state design, source/state separation and explicit human handoff rules.
Large revenue customers are not automatically desirable; real profit contribution and target appropriateness must be established before replication.
Interest without action is first a trigger/priority problem; copy should work backward from the desired observable transition.

The case contains four distinct checks: partner win, transaction-vs-structural type, revenue-share economics/risk and protection of borrowed trust. The previous baseline missed the structural distinction in both architectures.
Ability to pay and propensity to spend are distinct; customer economics still determines desirability.
Creative testing should exploit evidence from winners while keeping experiments interpretable and subordinate to real positioning/offering.
An event needs an observable response/follow-up and an audience whose economics justify the cost; current missed the latter in the frozen baseline.
